about: Tekken-style systems added to Street Fighter 6, offline only. One row per system. 'n/a' means the column does not apply to that row. Every cell must be filled. Heat follows Tekken 8: once per round, a 10 second timer that stops while the opponent is hit, no general damage bonus, and chip damage on block that cannot KO and that you win back by landing attacks. chip_pct_of_max and recover_pct_of_max_per_landed_attack are my estimates: Tekken's chip is 20% of the blocked attack's damage, which SF6 does not give us on a block yet. Rage follows Tekken 8 (season 3): active at 45 of 180 health (25%), +10% damage rounded down, and 70% less chip damage taken. A hit on a fighter who is not in Heat removes 30% of its damage from their recoverable health (from the Wavu wiki summary; whether the victim must be standing is not checked here).

rows.note: Tekken 8 Rage: at or under 25% health (45 of 180), every hit deals 10% more damage (rounded down) and chip damage taken is cut by 70%. Not possible here: Rage Art. The earlier numbers (20%, +15%) were verified working in game; these new numbers are untested.

Tekken 8 Heat: press the key (P1 F1 = 112, P2 F2 = 113) to start Heat. It can be used once per round and lasts 10 seconds of running time (600 match ticks, about 60 per second); the timer stops while the opponent is in hitstun. Heat gives no damage bonus. A blocked hit costs the blocker chip damage that cannot KO; it is recoverable and is won back when the chipped fighter lands attacks. Not possible here: Heat Smash, Heat Dash, Heat Burst (2+3) input and Engager moves. Earlier version (+15% damage, 20 second cooldown, permanent chip) was verified in game; this version is a redesign and is untested.
Tekken-style longer juggles by easing SF6's combo damage scaling. Not built: first find out what the probe says about combo_dm_air, and which data controls scaling.
